#     dplyr::mutate(d = high_ratio_low_victims_high_net_victims - low_ratio_high_victims_low_net_victims) %>%
#     ggplot (aes (x = 1, y = d)) +
#     theme_linedraw(14) +
#     geom_violin (alpha = .5,
#                  fill = "#5588CC",
#                  col="#5588CC") +
#     # ggplot2::scale_x_discrete("Response category",
#     #                  labels = ~ stringr::str_wrap(.x, 15),
#     #                  guide = guide_axis(angle = 60)) +
#     ggplot2::scale_y_continuous("Low victims - High Victims") +# , limits = 0:1) +
#     stat_summary(fun.data=mean_cl_boot,
#                  #fun.args = list(mult=sqrt (nlevels2(.$filename)-1)),
#                  geom="pointrange", color="#cc556f") +
#     geom_hline (yintercept = 0, lty = 3)
#


dat.moral.numbers %>%
    dplyr::filter(stringr::str_detect(experimentID, "exp3")) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(experimentID, ResponseId, conditionType, conditionPair) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(
        rating.raw = mean(rating.raw) - 3.5,
        rating.bin = mean(rating.bin)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
        names_from = c(conditionType),
        values_from = dplyr::starts_with("rating"),
        values_fill = NA_real_
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
        d.raw = dplyr::case_when(
            # Experiment 3
            !is.na(rating.raw_high_ratio_low_victims_high_net_victims) ~
                rating.raw_high_ratio_low_victims_high_net_victims -
                rating.raw_low_ratio_high_victims_low_net_victims,
            # Experiment 3b
            !is.na(rating.raw_high_ratio_low_victims_low_net_victims) ~
                rating.raw_high_ratio_low_victims_low_net_victims -
                rating.raw_low_ratio_high_victims_high_net_victims,
            TRUE ~ NA_real_
        ),
        d.bin = dplyr::case_when(
            # Experiment 3
            !is.na(rating.bin_high_ratio_low_victims_high_net_victims) ~
                rating.bin_high_ratio_low_victims_high_net_victims -
                rating.bin_low_ratio_high_victims_low_net_victims,
            # Experiment 3b
            !is.na(rating.bin_high_ratio_low_victims_low_net_victims) ~
                rating.bin_high_ratio_low_victims_low_net_victims -
                rating.bin_low_ratio_high_victims_high_net_victims,
            TRUE ~ NA_real_
        )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(-dplyr::starts_with("rating")) -> dat.moral.numbers.exp3.d.m

dplyr::bind_rows(
    dat.moral.numbers.exp3.d.m,
    dat.moral.numbers.exp3.d.m %>%
        dplyr::group_by(experimentID, ResponseId) %>%
        dplyr::summarize(
            d.raw = mean(d.raw),
            d.bin = mean(d.bin)
        ) %>%
        dplyr::mutate(conditionPair = "M")
) -> dat.moral.numbers.exp3.d.m
```

Orange circles represent individual participants."}

```{r exp3-descriptives}
dat.moral.numbers.exp3.d.m %>%
    dplyr::group_by(experimentID, conditionPair) %>%
    dplyr::summarize(dplyr::across(
        dplyr::starts_with("d"),
        list(
            N = length,
            M = mean,
            SE = se,
            "Cohen's" = ~ mean(.x) / se(.x),
            p = ~ wilcox.p(.x, mu = 0)
        )
    )) %>%
    dplyr::select(-d.bin_N) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::ends_with("_p"), fix_zero_p_values)) %>%
    kable.packed("experimentID",
                 caption = "Descriptives for Experiment 3 for the difference scores, using raw ratings and ratings transformed to binary variables. The p value reflects a Wilcoxon test against a chance level of zero. Positive differences reflect a preference for the high ratio/low victims condition.",
                 col.names = c(
                     "Pair", "N",
                     rep(c("M", "SE", "Cohen's d", "p"), 2)
                 ),
                 booktabs = TRUE
    ) %>%
    kableExtra::add_header_above(c(" " = 2, "Difference (raw)" = 4, "Difference (binary)" = 4), bold = TRUE) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(
        bootstrap_options = "striped",
        latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position", "repeat_header"), # , "scale_down"),
        full_width = TRUE
    ) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_classic_2()
```

## Unused: Correlations between ratios and difference scores

### Experiment 8

```{r exp8-asymptotic-vs-preasymptotic-range-raw-calculate-correlations}
dat.moral.numbers.exp8.asymptotic.vs.preasymptotic.raw.by.ratios <- dat.moral.numbers %>%
    dplyr::filter(
        stringr::str_starts(experimentID, "exp8"),
        question == "acceptability"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(experimentID, ratio, vivacity, ResponseId) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(rating = mean(rating.raw)) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
        id_cols = c(experimentID, ratio, ResponseId),
        names_from = vivacity,
        values_from = rating
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
        d.absolute = neutral - vivid,
        d.relative = 7 / 5 * (neutral - vivid) / (neutral + vivid)
    )

dat.moral.numbers.exp8.asymptotic.vs.preasymptotic.raw.by.ratios.correlations <-
    dat.moral.numbers.exp8.asymptotic.vs.preasymptotic.raw.by.ratios %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::starts_with("d."),
                        names_to = "difference.type",
                        values_to = "d"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(experimentID, difference.type) %>%
    rstatix::cor_test(d, ratio, method = "spearman")
```

```{r exp8-asymptotic-vs-preasymptotic-ratio-raw-correlation-plot, fig.cap = "Differences for raw ratings between the vivid and neutral condition as a function of ratios."}
dat.moral.numbers.exp8.asymptotic.vs.preasymptotic.raw.by.ratios %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::starts_with("d."),
                        names_to = "difference.type",
                        values_to = "d"
    ) %>%
    ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = ratio, y = d)) +
    stat_summary(
        fun.data = mean_cl_boot,
        geom = "pointrange"
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x) +
    # coord_trans(x = "log2") +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = l.moral.numbers.ratios$exp8,
        trans = "log2"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1)) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(experimentID ~ difference.type, scales = "free")
```

```{r exp8-asymptotic-vs-preasymptotic-ratio-raw-correlation-print}
dat.moral.numbers.exp8.asymptotic.vs.preasymptotic.raw.by.ratios.correlations %>%
    dplyr::select(experimentID, difference.type, cor, p) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(desc(experimentID), difference.type) %>%
    kable.packed(
        "experimentID",
        caption = "Correelations between ratios and difference scores of raw ratings between the vivid and the neutral conditions in Experiment 8.",
        # col.names = c(),
        linesep = "",
        booktabs = TRUE,
        longtable = FALSE,
        escape = FALSE
    ) %>%
    kableExtra::row_spec(9:12, color = "red") %>%
    # kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c(#"striped",
    #                                             #"hold_position",
    #                                             "scale_down")) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_classic_2()
```

The correlation coefficient between the ratios and the difference scores is always numerically negative. However, it reached only marginal significance when all participants were included, and when the relative difference score was used, but not in the other situations. As a result, it is unclear how to interpret these data. However, Figure \ref{fig:exp8-asymptotic-vs-preasymptotic-range-raw-plot} also shows that there is no clear relationship between ratio and difference score.
